title: Golden Tee
headline: Read the hole. Shape the swing.
intro: Golden Tee Fore! turns a bar-top trackball into a golf swing: roll back to set up, roll forward to strike, and shape the gesture to send the ball straight or bend it around a hazard. The pleasure is tactile judgment rather than a timed button press: the room watches the flight and reacts before the ball lands. Backspin, Fly-By and the setup buttons make a short pause between shots part of the game, not dead time.

referenceScope.primary: Golden Tee Fore! (Incredible Technologies coin-op, Fore! family)
referenceScope.reason: Fore! is the generation this build's own research already treats as the legacy MAME bench candidate (romset gtfore06); its own manual, flyer and a native gtfore06 screenshot give primary-source control and on-screen detail instead of a different generation.
referenceScope.caveat: No release is selected and no game was run here. Sources span two Fore! sub-builds — a circa-2001 cabinet/flyer and 2006 Complete gameplay screenshots — not confirmed as one identical build; the 1995-documented swing mechanic is carried forward, not re-confirmed per sub-build. Full detail in Release Notes.

session.format: Stroke or Skins play across 9 or 18 holes, one to four golfers alternating turns at one trackball panel; Start plus a roll-to-highlight doubles as the in-round menu for Instant Replay, Mulligan purchase, and Skip Turn.
session.social: Players wait their turn at the shared panel and call the shot — hook, slice, over-hit — as the swing starts, the way a gallery reads a real golfer's takeaway; Skip Turn lets a player who isn't ready get passed over instead of holding up the hole.
session.failureToAvoid: A trackball that drops counts on a fast swing, or a Start+roll menu that misreads a mistimed stroke as a shot, breaks this shared, call-it rhythm.

playLoop.title: Scout the hole and set a line
playLoop.action: Use Fly-By to preview the hole from tee to green, choose a target line and orient your hand before starting the swing.
playLoop.feedback: The preview reveals the route; the course view and overhead map show the lie, hazards and direction toward the pin.

playLoop.title: Arm Backspin before you need it
playLoop.action: Press Backspin before the swing; press again before swinging to cancel.
playLoop.feedback: Backspin is armed before the shot; a suitable struck shot can check up or roll back. A prominent armed-state badge is proposed feedback, not a HUD element verified here.
playLoop.skill: Planning spin ahead of a shot, not reacting after it lands.

playLoop.title: Back swing sets power and shape
playLoop.action: Roll backward along your aim line for straight, or off-angle from the landing direction for a hook or slice.
playLoop.feedback: The golfer coils into a backswing matching the distance — not speed — of the roll.
playLoop.skill: Back-swing distance is one of two independent inputs; its speed is explicitly irrelevant.

playLoop.title: Forward swing strikes the ball
playLoop.action: Roll forward with real velocity, pushing toward the direction you want the ball to start heading.
playLoop.feedback: The golfer swings through; too much velocity triggers over-hitting, a loss of control rather than extra distance.
playLoop.skill: Controlling velocity instead of maximizing it.

playLoop.title: Read the next lie before swinging again
playLoop.action: After the ball settles, check the updated club-and-yardage capsule and, on an approach, the slope-of-the-green overhead map before repeating the back-swing/forward-swing shot.
playLoop.feedback: The capsule and map update to the new lie, giving a fresh target before the next roll.
playLoop.skill: Treat every shot as its own read, not a repeat of the tee shot.

playLoop.title: Putt out
playLoop.action: On the green, read the slope map and use the same back-swing/forward-swing trackball gesture at putting scale to finish the hole.
playLoop.feedback: A holed putt ends the hole; a miss leaves a shorter putt and one more stroke.
playLoop.skill: Reading green break from the overhead map instead of guessing the line.

screenRead.label: Wind arrow + MPH readout
screenRead.meaning: Current wind direction/strength, one of the three checks before every swing.

screenRead.label: Club + distance capsule
screenRead.meaning: Selected club and flagged yardage together, read to pick a club before rolling back.

screenRead.label: Stroke counter
screenRead.meaning: Running stroke count for the hole — the simplest ‘how am I doing’ readout.

screenRead.label: Slope-of-the-green overhead map
screenRead.meaning: A cutaway map of the green's break, read before an approach or putt to anticipate the roll.

screenRead.label: Proposed Backspin status
screenRead.meaning: A clear armed/cancelled status would confirm the documented pre-shot Backspin control. This badge is a presentation proposal, not an original HUD element established by the manual.

gameplayStoryboard.summary: Follow a hole from tee setup to putt and result. Fore!'s five-button panel is the control reference; the older Golden Tee 3D manual explains backswing amount plus forward-roll speed as the power inputs. Confirm that inherited behavior on the exact Fore! build before implementation. Camera direction, continuous shot tracking and new status feedback below are proposed presentation, not features proved in our own working game.

stages.title: Tee box: read the hole, preview the line
stages.playerAction: Golfer addresses the ball at the tee. Player reads the wind arrow/MPH, club-and-yardage capsule and stroke counter, then presses Fly-By to preview the route from tee to green before committing to an aim line.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: over-the-shoulder tee camera centered on the golfer's stance with the hole corridor receding toward the green; cuts to a following shot during the Fly-By preview.
onScreen: Wind arrow + MPH readout (documented HUD, GT1/GT6)
Fly-By route preview triggered by the Fly-By button (documented control, GT3)
stages.feedback: Fly-By traces the hole so the player commits to a target line with the hazards already seen, not guessed at.
stages.decision: Player picks an aim line and decides whether to pre-arm Backspin for the shot about to be struck.

stages.title: Arm Backspin, then shape the backswing
stages.playerAction: Optionally press Backspin before the swing; press again to cancel. Roll the trackball backward to set the backswing. In the older Golden Tee 3D manual, backswing amount contributes to shot power, while backswing speed does not; the forward roll supplies the other power input. Backward and forward directions shape the shot. Verify the exact Fore! behavior at the bench.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: low tee-side angle holding on the golfer's takeaway, matching the real-time arc of the trackball roll so the shape being set is readable.
onScreen: Proposed Backspin armed/cancelled badge for the documented pre-shot control
Proposed clear backswing-depth animation; the amount-versus-speed distinction comes from the older Golden Tee 3D manual
Keep the tactile trackball gesture rather than substitute an unproven timing-bar mini-game
stages.feedback: The golfer's backswing depth visibly matches the roll distance; an off-axis roll visibly cants the swing plane toward hook or slice.
stages.decision: Player commits to a shot shape — straight, hook or slice — and a planned swing depth before the forward roll begins.

stages.title: Forward swing strikes the ball
stages.playerAction: Player rolls the trackball forward with real velocity, pushing toward the direction the ball should start heading. Velocity sets power; excess velocity triggers over-hitting, a loss of control rather than extra distance.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: impact-moment camera crossing from the downswing to a close framing on clubface-to-ball contact, then releasing to follow the launch.
onScreen: Golfer's swing-through animation keyed to the forward roll's measured velocity (documented mechanic, GT4)
An over-hit result shown distinctly from a clean strike when forward velocity is excessive (documented failure mode, GT4)
Wind, club/yardage and stroke-counter HUD remain visible through the swing (documented HUD, GT1/GT6)
stages.feedback: A clean strike launches the ball on the shape set in the previous stage; an over-hit visibly loses accuracy regardless of that shape.
stages.decision: The committed swing shape and velocity are locked in — there is no redo once the forward roll registers.

stages.title: Ball flight: shape, spin and wind play out
stages.playerAction: No input during flight. The player watches the shaped shot, any armed backspin, and the wind read at address pull the ball toward or away from the target line chosen at the tee.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: continuous chase camera following the ball from strike through apex to descent, holding the hole's hazards in frame so the shaped flight reads against the dogleg, bunker or water the player aimed around.
onScreen: Ball trajectory continuing unbroken from the forward-strike launch point (presentation continuity, not a cataloged original HUD element)
Wind arrow/MPH readout remaining visible, unchanged from the tee-setup read (documented HUD, GT1/GT6)
A hook or slice bending the flight around an obstacle a straight shot could not clear, per the manufacturer's own technique guide (GT4)
stages.feedback: The flight path confirms or punishes the shape call made before swinging — a bent shot that clears a hazard, or a straight shot that was supposed to bend and didn't.
stages.decision: None for the player; this stage pays off the shape and power decisions already made and sets up the next lie.

stages.title: Landing: read the next lie
stages.playerAction: Ball settles. Player reads the updated club-and-yardage capsule and, on an approach, the slope-of-the-green overhead map to judge the next shot's break before rolling back again.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: cut to the ball's resting position with the green or next landing zone in the background, matching the overhead-map framing to the live camera angle.
onScreen: Updated club + yardage capsule reflecting the new lie (documented HUD, GT1/GT6)
Slope-of-the-green overhead map, shown when the approach is within range of the green (documented HUD, GT1/GT6)
Stroke counter incremented by one (documented HUD, GT1/GT6)
stages.feedback: The new yardage and visible lie tell the player whether the prior shot's shape call paid off.
stages.decision: Player selects a new target line and shot shape, repeating the backswing/strike stages, or proceeds to putting if already on the green.

stages.title: Putting: read the break, roll out, see the result
stages.playerAction: On the green, the player reads the slope-of-the-green overhead map, then uses the same back-swing/forward-swing trackball gesture at putting scale to roll the ball at the hole.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: low green-level camera tracking the ball's roll toward the cup, with the overhead slope map available as a cutaway inset.
onScreen: Stroke counter finalizing the hole's score (documented HUD, GT1/GT6)
Hole result — holed or missed, with the ball's resting distance if missed
stages.feedback: A holed putt ends the hole and banks the stroke count; a missed putt leaves a shorter next putt and one more stroke on the counter.
stages.decision: Player reads the green's break and commits to a line and a backswing-to-forward-roll ratio informed by the slope map rather than guesswork. Putt-specific input calibration is not independently confirmed in the sourced Fore! manual and needs verification against the selected build.

signatureMoments.title: The hook around the dogleg
signatureMoments.description: Pull back off-axis from where you want the ball to land, push forward toward where you want it to start — the exact technique in the manufacturer's own tips guide, bending a drive around an obstacle a straight shot can't clear.

signatureMoments.title: The backswing-skipped recovery
signatureMoments.description: A player can skip the back swing entirely and still strike the ball, at a real power penalty — a built-in recovery for a fumbled roll that keeps a first-timer in the game.

signatureMoments.title: Calling the shot from the rail
signatureMoments.description: Design interpretation: because the swing gesture is the one unmistakable motion at the panel, onlookers can read its angle and depth and call hook, slice, or over-hit before the ball lands.

controls.action: Sets shot shape and supplies the first of two power inputs; back-swing speed is explicitly irrelevant.
controls.feel: A loose, free-spinning roll with real travel, not a flick — must track an off-axis roll as faithfully as a straight one.

controls.action: Strikes the ball; velocity sets power, with over-hitting a named failure mode for excess force.
controls.feel: Needs a fast, uninterrupted roll with no dropped counts, or a good swing reads back as weak.

controls.action: Pre-arms backspin before the swing; press again to cancel.
controls.feel: A single confident press during setup, not a hold or a post-shot reaction.

controls.action: Previews the hole's layout from tee to green before the swing.
controls.feel: A quick look-before-you-leap beat between aiming and swinging.

controls.action: The current manufacturer's guide documents golfer rotation. Fore!'s manual also documents a leaderboard-scrolling use; exact in-play behavior and degrees per press must be checked on the selected Fore! build.
controls.feel: Keep both setup buttons available; do not import a later release's rotation increments or held-button mode without verification.

buildPriorities.title: Sample the swing, not just the click
buildPriorities.why: Two numbers — peak back-swing distance, peak forward-swing velocity — come from one roll; dropped counts invent phantom weak or over-hit shots unrelated to skill.
buildPriorities.proof: A full sweep of the documented swing-speed range gives correct, undropped readings at the fastest rolls a guest actually throws.

buildPriorities.title: Keep the five-button panel intact
buildPriorities.why: Fore!'s panel is Start, Backspin, Fly-By, Left, Right; a trimmed panel cannot pre-arm backspin or preview a hole as the reference manual describes.
buildPriorities.proof: A first-time guest can arm Backspin and preview with Fly-By without hunting for a hidden control.

buildPriorities.title: Don't let the menu steal the swing
buildPriorities.why: Start+roll drives both the shot and the in-round menu; a mistimed roll during a menu can look identical to a swing input.
buildPriorities.proof: A guest can use Mulligan or Skip Turn and then take a real shot back-to-back without an accidental double input.

buildPriorities.title: Give the off-axis roll real room
buildPriorities.why: The hook/slice technique needs an angled roll read as faithfully as a straight one; a cramped panel or stiff bearing flattens the curve.
buildPriorities.proof: A player can reliably bend a shot around a visible obstacle using the documented pull-back/push-forward-off-axis technique.

releaseNotes.title: Fore! is not 3D Golf, LIVE/PGA TOUR, or the Remastered Edition
releaseNotes.body: This page documents the Fore! family: five buttons (Start, Backspin, Fly-By, Left, Right) with a dedicated pre-arm Backspin button. 3D Golf gets backspin from swing technique alone, no button. Current LIVE/PGA TOUR cabinets and the factory Fore! Remastered Edition home cabinet are later, separate generations with their own courses and UI — neither is pictured or described here.

releaseNotes.title: Left/Right's exact behavior is generation-specific
releaseNotes.body: The manufacturer's current guide documents Left/Right as rotating the golfer in fixed degrees on the modern LIVE-era UI. The Fore!-era manual used here instead documents Left/Right (with Fly-By) as controlling scroll speed/direction while browsing leaderboard info after a card swipe. Both are real, documented uses on different generations — don't assume one carries to the other.

releaseNotes.title: This gallery spans two Fore! sub-builds
releaseNotes.body: The cabinet, control-panel and brochure photographs document an early Fore! unit (2001 flyer; archived cabinet circa 2002). The two gameplay screenshots are a native capture of the MAME gtfore06 romset, ‘Golden Tee Fore! 2006 Complete (v6.00.01)’ — a later Fore! sub-build. The five-button layout is confirmed consistent across both; course art and HUD styling differ between the two eras pictured. The back-swing/forward-swing power rule itself is documented for the earlier 1995 3D Golf generation and treated as carried into Fore! because Fore!'s own manual assumes it as already known — it is not independently re-confirmed in print for every individual Fore! sub-build shown here.
